title: A neural network won ImageNet 2012 by about ten points
summary: In the 2012 ImageNet contest, a deep convolutional network from the University of Toronto reached a 15.3% top-5 error rate, compared with 26.2% for the second-best entry. The contest report called the team the undisputed winner.

beats.say: One neural network won an image contest by roughly ten points.
beats.cap: A neural network won by ~10 points

beats.say: The ImageNet contest asked programs to name objects in photos.
beats.cap: Name the object in each photo

beats.say: It used one thousand categories and about one point two million training images.
A guess counted as right if the answer was among five labels.
The winning network came from the University of Toronto.
It had sixty million parameters and trained on two graphics cards.
It scored fifteen point three percent error, and the runner up twenty six point two.
The contest report called that team the undisputed winner.
It was a large, deep convolutional neural network trained on pixel values.
Same contest, same test, a gap of roughly ten points.

claims.note: AlexNet paper abstract: '26.2% achieved by the second-best entry'; ILSVRC report Table 5 lists ISI at 26.2%
AlexNet paper abstract: a variant entered in ILSVRC-2012 achieved a winning top-5 test error rate of 15.3% (the ILSVRC report's Table 5 lists SuperVision at 16.4%)
ILSVRC report: approximately 1.2 million training images
AlexNet paper: the network has 60 million parameters
AlexNet paper: trained on two NVIDIA GTX 580 3GB GPUs; training took 5-6 days

facts.claim: The 2012 ImageNet classification task used 1000 object classes and about 1.2 million training images
facts.note: ILSVRC report (arXiv 1409.0575), Section 3.1.4: '1000 object classes and approximately 1.2 million training images'

facts.claim: A prediction counts as correct if the right label is among five guesses (top-5 error)
facts.note: ILSVRC report, Section 4.1: an algorithm may return five labels and is considered correct if the ground-truth label appears among them

facts.claim: The AlexNet paper reports a winning top-5 test error of 15.3% in ILSVRC-2012 against 26.2% for the second-best entry; the work was done at the University of Toronto
facts.note: AlexNet paper abstract: 'winning top-5 test error rate of 15.3%, compared to 26.2% achieved by the second-best entry'; prologue: 'while we were at the University of Toronto'

facts.claim: The official ILSVRC report lists SuperVision at 16.4% and ISI at 26.2%, and calls SuperVision the undisputed winner of 2012
facts.note: ILSVRC report: Table 5 lists SuperVision (University of Toronto) at 16.4% and ISI at 26.2%; text: 'The undisputed winner of both the classification and localization tasks in 2012 was the SuperVision team'. The gap is about ten points on either figure (9.8 or 10.9)

facts.claim: The network had 60 million parameters and trained for 5-6 days on two NVIDIA GTX 580 GPUs
facts.note: AlexNet paper: 60 million parameters; two GTX 580 3GB GPUs; 5-6 days of training
